question.text: Ulaanbaatar is the capital of this Asian country, the center of a former empire led by Genghis Khan.
question.clue: The prince Kul Tigin is honored by 7th century inscriptions named for a river valley in this country's west, the Orkhon, which was a power center for the Gokturk state.

swap.leadin: This group mocked the US, France, and UK forces during a mock funeral in Khost.
swap.text: Name this group that took over a certain country after defeating a resistance movement in Panjshir Province. This group, which takes its name from the word "students," is largely led by Pashtun militants.
swap.clue: This group, the main opponent of the Northern Alliance, carried out the "green on blue" attacks.

question.leadin: Give the following about the 1449 Tumu [tuh-MU] Crisis.
question.text: The crisis involved a raid of 20,000 of these people, led by Esen Taishi, into Ming territory where they destroyed an unprepared army of half a million Ming soldiers. These people ruled the Yuan Dynasty, which was defeated by the Ming.
question.clue: Previously, at the battle of the Kalka River, these people used the tactic of feigned retreat to achieve victory while led by Subutai.

swap.leadin: The beginning of this war in 1979 led US president Jimmy Carter to boycott the 1980 Olympics in Moscow. --.
swap.text: Identify this conflict between a communist power and a central Asian nation. The C.I.A. supplied the mujahedeen during this conflict.
swap.clue: Operation Cyclone was an effort to fund one side in this conflict through the operation of the ISI, and was heavily promoted by men like Gust Avrakotos.

question.leadin: This Turkic conqueror of the 1300s won the Battle of Ankara in 1402.
question.text: Name this ruler and general who conquered Central Asia, Persia, and parts of the Middle East in his quest to restore the Mongol Khanate.
question.clue: After detaining an envoy sent by the Emperor Hongwu, he led a short lived expedition against the Ming Dynasty.

swap.leadin: Lord Elphinstone's army was massacred by Wazir Khan during a retreat from this country's capital.
swap.text: Name this country where the Durrani family ruled from a palace in Kabul. The CIA supported the Mujahideen during a Soviet invasion of this country in 1979.
swap.clue: One invasion of this country was ended by the Treaty of Gandamak and took place during the "Great Game."

question.leadin: Answer these questions about successor states to the Mongol empire of Genghis Khan.
question.text: Alexander Nevsky allied with this polity in modern-day Russia, whose distinctive tents arose after Orda and Batu Khan's Blue and White factions merged. It lost at Kulikovo, and Tokhtamysh led it while fighting Tamerlane.
question.clue: Mamai's successor Tokhtamysh fought Timur, and it long had a capital at Sarai Berke.

swap.leadin: This man served as Afghanistan's head of state for five years until 2001.
swap.text: Name this man who died of tuberculosis in 2013 but was only officially declared dead in summer 2015, when he was succeeded by Akhtar Mansoor.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a certain country.
question.text: Primarily made up of three groups the Uzbeks, the Hazara, and the Tajiks, members of this military and political organization aided in overthrowing the Taliban and found key positions in Hamid Karzai's government.
question.answerHtml: The Northern Alliance [or The United Front for the Salvation of Afghanistan; or the UIF]

swap.leadin: This empire was founded by the son of a general who served Nader Shah Afshar.
swap.text: Name this empire, which controlled Afghanistan from the mid 1700s to the mid 1800s. This empire was founded by Ahmad Shah Abdali.
swap.clue: This empire briefly established itself as the preeminent power of northwest South Asia following its victory over the Maratha Confederacy at the Third Battle of Panipat.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of a mountainous nation that's been in the news a lot.
question.text: In 1893, the British set up this border between Afghanistan and Pakistan based on geographical features, not ethnic regions. This idiotic idea continues to lend itself today to ethnic tensions.
question.clue: The creation of this line, named for a British diplomat, effectively created a buffer zone between Britain and Russia in Asia. This line forms the de facto border between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

swap.text: Centuries after al-Razi, this ruler's grandson Ulugh Beg sponsored Persian scholars in several hospitals and observatories. This Turco-Mongol conqueror created several pyramids of skulls and walked with a limp.
swap.answerHtml: Timur [or Tamerlane or Tamburlaine; or Timur the Lame or Timur Lenk or Timur-i Lang; or Temür Küregen or Timūr Gurkānī; accept Timurid Empire or Timurid dynasty or the Timurids or Gūrkāniyān]
swap.clue: The only time an Ottoman Sultan was captured in battle was duringthis man's victory at the Battle of Ankara against Bayezid Thunderbolt.

question.leadin: The BMAC is sometimes called the [this river] civilization, despite the fact that most of its sites were instead found around the Margiana.
question.text: Name this river which separated the historical regions of Sogdiana and Bactria. A region named for being beyond this river was north of the ancient province of Khorasan.
question.clue: A golden fish and a model chariot are among many items in an Achaemenid-era "treasure" named for this river.

swap.leadin: In his 2002 "Trashcanistan" article, Stephen Kotkin argues that this country is the only post-Soviet Central Asian state to not depend on Russia.
swap.text: Name this former Soviet Republic whose leader Rafiq Nishabov was removed by Moscow in 1989 after failing to stop ethnic violence against this country's Meskhetian Turks, which culminated in the Fergana massacre.
swap.answerHtml: Uzbekistan [or Republic of Uzbekistan; accept Oʻzbekiston Respublikasi; accept Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic or Uzbek SSR or Uzbekskaja Sovetskaja Socialističeskaja Respublika or Oʻzbekiston Sovet Sotsialistik Respublikasi; accept Uzbekia]
swap.clue: In one event in this country, Chulpon Avenue was closed and hundred of people in Bobur Square were killed in a protest blamed on the Islamic group Akramia.

question.leadin: Of the 16,000-plus men to begin a journey from this city, only assistant surgeon William Brydon survived to reach Jalalabad (juh-LAHL-uh-bad).
question.text: Name this city from which Lord Elphinstone led a disastrous retreat in 1842. In modern times, the Saur (SAH-wur) Revolution ended after Sardar Daud Khan was assassinated in this capital city.
question.clue: Leaving from Khanadar, this city was captured by Ahmad Shah Durrani whose son Timur Shah moved the capital of their empire to this city in 1772.

swap.text: The Eastern Turkic Khaganate was formed from this group who were led by the Ashina clan and formed a namesake Khaganate after succeeding the Rouran ("ROH-ran").
swap.answerHtml: Göktürks [or Blue Turks or Celestial Turks or Tūjué; accept Göktürk Khaganate]

question.text: The Gokturks were led by this tribe and ruling dynasty. This tribe had been subjugated by the Rouran in 460, but conquered them in 552 under the leadership of Bumin Qaghan.

swap.leadin: In his article "The Last Good Chance", Peter Krause contrasted this battle with the later Operation Anaconda and argued that American objectives could have been achieved through the use of a significant number of block and sweep troops.
swap.text: Identify this battle fought in the White Mountains, part of Operation Enduring Freedom.

question.leadin: The Rajputs defeated a ruler of this dynasty at the First Battle of Taraori, so he raised a bigger army, revised his tactics, went back the next year, and crushed them on the same battlefield.
question.text: Identify this Persianate dynasty, originally from a namesake region in present-day Afghanistan, whose ruler Mu'izz ad-Din Muhammad conquered the Ghaznavids by capturing Lahore in 1186 CE.

swap.leadin: A member of this family abolished the longstanding beylik system in a series of westernizing reforms encouraged by his backer Catherine the Great.
swap.text: Name this family whose founder supposedly devised a three-pronged symbol known as the Tarak Tamga. That man's son defeated the last Khan of the Golden Horde and occupied Sarai.
swap.answerHtml: Giray [accept Hacı I Giray or Melek Haji Giray or Şahin Giray]
